title: An afternoon in family medicine
intro: Clinical Immersion: one to four in the afternoon in the hospital's outpatient clinics, with a family physician and a full schedule.

steps.say: "Twenty-minute visits, one to four problems each. Family medicine is everything, for everyone, over years. Come on, room 3 is waiting."
steps.speaker: Dr. Grace Whitfield, family physician

steps.say: Room 3: Mr. Davis, 54, back for his blood pressure. His home readings are in the 150s over 90s on amlodipine.
Your reading: 152/94, the same as his home readings. Dr. Whitfield raises his amlodipine dose, and you both go through his salt intake, in great detail.
Room 5: Ms. Alvarez, 32, tired all the time. Her blood tests from last month are normal.

steps.question: imm_fm_phq2_01
steps.lead: "Before we order more tests, screen her."

steps.say: She scores 5 on the PHQ-2. On the PHQ-9 she scores 16, and then she says something that makes the room go quiet.

choice.prompt: "Sometimes I think everyone would be better off without me." Dr. Whitfield has stepped out to take a call. You:

options.text: Ask calmly and directly: "Are you having thoughts of ending your life?" Then make sure Dr. Whitfield hears it before anyone leaves.
options.reply: She has had the thoughts, but no plan. Dr. Whitfield comes straight back; they make a safety plan together, with the crisis line number and a visit next week.

options.text: Change the subject to something more hopeful.
options.reply: The moment passes, and the risk goes unassessed.

options.text: Reassure her that everyone feels that way sometimes.
options.reply: She goes quiet. She feels dismissed.

choice.lesson: Asking directly about suicide doesn't put the idea in someone's head; it's how you find the risk and get help

steps.say: Room 2: Mr. Price, 45, here for a cough, a pack a day for thirty years.

choice.prompt: "I know I should quit. But it's the only thing that relaxes me."

options.text: "It sounds like smoking does something important for you, and part of you wants to quit. What would be different if you did?"
options.reply: He thinks about it. "I could play with my granddaughter without coughing." Now he's the one making the case.

options.text: "You need to quit. Smoking causes cancer and heart disease."
"Maybe try cutting down to half a pack?"

choice.lesson: Use open questions and reflections (motivational interviewing) so patients voice their own reasons to change

steps.question: imm_fm_quit_01
steps.lead: He sets a quit date. "What should we offer him?"

steps.say: At four o'clock, Dr. Whitfield signs your form. "You'll see all of these again: in the hospital, in the ED, in every specialty. This is where they start."

feedback: Dr. Whitfield writes: "Calm, kind and safe. You asked the hard question. Excellent."
Dr. Whitfield writes: "Engaged and thoughtful. Keep practicing the open questions."
Dr. Whitfield writes: "A good first clinic. Read about depression screening and MI tonight."
